title: Attestation-aware Secrets Gateway roadmap and terraform notes
content:
Purpose:

This draft defines the design and staged rollout plan for an "attestation-aware" secrets gateway for private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. The gateway centralizes secret distribution and enforces hardware-backed key operations (HSM/KMS) combined with node attestation. The focus is operational hardening: key management patterns, secrets lifecycle, terraform module recommendations, upgrade and rollback procedures, and audit/logging requirements for compliance.

Goals:
- Provide a single control plane for secrets that can interoperate with customer-managed HSMs (on-prem or cloud) and our KMS adapter.
- Enforce attestation-based release of DEKs to runtime nodes (VMs / containers) to ensure only verified hosts can unwrap keys.
- Minimize blast radius when migrating keys or upgrading modules; provide clear terraform migration steps and rollbacks.
- Produce tamper-evident audit trails and integrate with existing observability pipelines.

Non-goals:
- Implementing full PKI for customer environments (we rely on existing attestation providers: TPM, Nitro Enclaves, or GCP/AWS attestation services).
- Replacing customer HSM vendors; focus on interop and fallback.

High-level architecture (textual):
- Secrets Gateway (SG): stateless control plane deployed in customer VPC; authenticates operator and clusters, stores metadata only.
- KEK Manager: interacts with customer KMS/HSM via configured connectors (cloud KMS, network HSM, HSM appliance over PKCS#11). Holds only KEK references, not plaintext DEKs.
- DEK Store (encrypted): encrypted blob store (object store or vault) in customer environment; encrypted under KEK.
- Attestation Service: verifies node identity and health (TPM quote, cloud attestation token) and issues a short-lived attestation credential used to request DEK unwrapping.
- Secrets Agent (on node): requests DEKs from SG after presenting attestation token and mTLS identity; caches DEKs in memory with TTL + automatic wipe on signals.

Key flows:
1) Provisioning: Operator registers KEK connector in SG with PKCS#11 URI, connector credentials, key ID. Terraform-managed resource: redwood_secrets_kek_connector.
2) Secret write: Operator uploads secret to SG API; SG generates DEK (random), encrypts secret with DEK, calls KEK Manager to wrap DEK -> stores wrapped DEK + ciphertext in DEK store.
3) Node fetch: Node performs attestation -> obtains attestation token -> mTLS to SG -> SG validates attestation / policy -> asks KEK Manager to unwrap DEK (transient) -> returns plaintext DEK to SG just long enough to encrypt transport to node (or uses ECDH established session) -> node receives and decrypts secret locally.
4) Rotation: Operator triggers key rotation; new DEK generation and rewrap. Support rolling rewrap without downtime via dual-KEK acceptance window.

Operational hardening patterns:
- Always prefer HSM for KEK operations; configure offline HSM policies for high-sensitivity KEKs.
- Use split knowledge / dual-operator approval for KEK rotations on production class secrets.
- Enforce short attestation token lifetimes (<= 30s) and single-use tokens where backend supports it.
- Secrets Agent must zero memory on SIGTERM and provide explicit API to purge memory on SIGKILL tolerant platforms.
- Use envelope encryption: SG never persists plaintext DEKs to disk. Logs must redact all DEK plaintext.

Terraform module notes (recommendations):
- Module name: redwood/secrets-gateway/aws (or /gcp /onprem depending on provider). Keep provider-specific pieces behind small wrapper modules.
- Versioning: Semver for modules. Breaking changes only on major bump.
- Resources to expose:
  - variables: keystore_connector (object/string ref), deks_bucket (string), attestation_provider (enum), node_agent_config (map), audit_sink (string), admin_principals (list).
  - outputs: gateway_url, sg_service_account, kek_connector_id, audit_sink_id.
- Example minimal variables block for terraform uses (text snippet):
  variable \"keystore_connector\" { type = string }
  variable \"deks_bucket\" { type = string }
  variable \"attestation_provider\" { type = string }
- Important: implement "import" helpers (terraform import) for existing KEKs and DEK blobs. Provide a migration script that imports existing SecretsGateway state into the module state: scripts/terraform/import_existing_keys.sh (see migration steps below).
- Lock provider versions and add explicit lifecycle rules to prevent accidental destroy: lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } on critical resources when env == "prod".

Upgrade and migration plan (high level):
- Preconditions: backups of wrapped-DEK blobs, KEK connector configuration exported, snapshot of SG configuration, full test suite passing in staging.
- Stage 1 (canary): Deploy new module to staging namespace; run end-to-end test where node attestation -> fetch -> decrypt cycle is exercised with staged HSM connector. Verify audit entries and metrics.
- Stage 2 (pilot): Deploy to one customer tenant (non-critical) or to one AZ within customer VPC. Use traffic shaping to limit live traffic and increase observability.
- Stage 3 (gradual rollout): For each customer region, perform a rolling gateway update with the following steps per region:
  1) terraform plan and review.
  2) terraform apply in canary subnet (1 instance). Verify attestation flow.
  3) Run rewrap test: generate test secret, rotate DEK, verify both old and new DEKs valid within acceptance window.
  4) Increase SG replicas and switch traffic.
  5) Remove old connectors after confirmation window.
- Rollback plan: keep previous module version in a branch that can be applied quickly. If unwrapping starts failing, immediately reverse to previous version and run a reconciliation script that rewraps any DEKs that were rekeyed under new KEK back to previous KEK, using backed-up plaintext OR via HSM facilitate multi-wrap (if available).

Terraform-specific migration steps (detailed):
- Step 0: Export current state: aws s3 cp s3://<deks-bucket>/metadata/backup-YYYYMMDD.json ./backup.json
- Step 1: Map existing KEKs to new terraform resource ids: create a mapping file (keystone-map.csv) with columns: existing_key_id, provider, suggested_tf_id.
- Step 2: Use terraform import for each KEK connector: terraform import module.sg.redwood_kek_connector["<tf_id>"] <existing_key_id>
- Step 3: For DEK blobs: if module maintains list objects, import via terraform import aws_s3_object.dek["<blob_name>"] <bucket>/<path>
- Step 4: Apply plan in dry-run mode: terraform plan -var-file=pilot.tfvars -out=pilot.plan
- Step 5: Apply: terraform apply pilot.plan
- Step 6: Run smoke tests and audit checks.

Secrets lifecycle acceptance tests (smoke checklist):
- Write secret -> read from node agent -> verify plaintext matches.
- Force attestation failure (tamper test) -> ensure secrets not returned.
- Rotate KEK -> ensure old DEKs still decrypt during acceptance window.
- Simulate HSM unavailability -> verify fallback policy: either deny unwrapping or use secondary KEK only if explicitly permitted.
- Verify audit entry emitted for every wrap/unwrap with fields: operation, subject (node id or operator id), timestamp, kek_id, secret_id, attestation_status.

Audit & logging requirements:
- Structured audit events (JSON): include event_id, operation, actor, subject_id, kek_id, attestation_result, outcome, request_id. Do not include plaintext or raw DEKs.
- Tamper-evident ledger: support streaming of audit events to a write-once object store or append-only service (configurable by customer). Provide optional signed checkpoint metadata for periodic snapshots.
- Retention: default 90 days hot, 1 year cold; customer config override supported via module variable.
- Integrations: ELK (Logstash -> ES), Splunk HEC, and syslog. Provide example fluent-bit config blocks in the module docs.
- Alerts: alert if unwrap failure rate > 0.5% in 5m window or if abnormal spike in rotation operations.

HSM/KMS interop considerations and edge cases:
- PKCS#11 vs Cloud KMS APIs: provide adapter layer. PKCS#11 connectors must run in a hardened subnet and use mTLS to SG.
- Network HSM latency: add retry/backoff in KEK manager and avoid blocking attestation path for more than 10s.
- Multi-KMS setups: support multi-wrap (wrap DEK under multiple KEKs) to allow migration with zero-downtime fallback. Document the increased storage and complexity costs.
- Attestation dropout: if attestation provider temporarily fails, do not fallback to unconditional unwrapping. Use configurable emergency procedure requiring operator approval recorded in the audit log.

Observability metrics (suggested):
- secrets_gateway.requests.total, secrets_gateway.unwrap.success, secrets_gateway.wrap.success, secrets_gateway.attestation.failures, secrets_gateway.kms.latency_seconds (p95,p99), secrets_gateway.memory_dek_cache_size.
- Tag metrics by customer_tenant, region, kek_id. Export to Prometheus and set SLOs: unwrap latency p95 < 200ms (local HSM), p95 < 1.5s (network HSM).

Security checklist (pre-deploy):
- [ ] KEK connectors validated with test keys in staging HSM.
- [ ] Terraform module with prevent_destroy in prod-critical resources.
- [ ] Audit sink configured and smoke-tested.
- [ ] Attestation provider integration verified (TPM quotes validated in staging nodes).
- [ ] Secrets Agent signed binaries and reproducible build provenance available.

Open questions / risks:
- Can all customer HSMs support transient unwrap operations without exposing DEK? (some older appliances may require adaptations).
- How to handle air-gapped customers who cannot reach our attestation CA? Proposed: provide local CA distribution and offline attestation mode but requires operator approval and manual audit steps.
- Customer regulatory needs for longer audit retention or different storage location. Module needs retention config per-tenant.

Next actions / owners:
- Prototype adapter for PKCS#11 node -> Diego (due 2024-12-10).
- Create terraform import helper scripts and docs -> Linnea (due 2024-12-05).
- Build staged canary runbook with exact tests -> Marcus (due 2024-12-08).
- Run tabletop for rollback scenarios with SRE -> Asha (due 2024-12-01).

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Example import command for KEK connector:
  terraform import module.sg.redwood_kek_connector["cust-onprem-hsm-01"] pkcs11://token-label/key-id-0

- Example smoke curl (node requesting secret):
  curl -v -k --cert node-agent.crt --key node-agent.key \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <attestation-token>" \
    https://secrets-gateway.internal/v1/secrets/read?name=service/a/postgres

- Minimal fluent-bit output config for audit sink (example):
  [OUTPUT]
  Name  es
  Match secrets-gateway.audits
  Host  elk-logging.local
  Port  9200
  Type  _doc

End of draft.
